facts.statement: The study asks whether the need for the RIM protein is the same at all synapses that have different natural release probabilities.
facts.subject: computational

facts.statement: The researchers used a neurotoxin to silence specific nerve inputs in fruit flies to test the role of RIM.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: Removing RIM stopped nerve signals at the fast, high-release synapse but did not stop signals at the slow, low-release synapse nearby.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: The protein is needed for short-term signal strengthening at the fast synapse but not for long-term strengthening at the slow synapse.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: High-resolution pictures showed the RIM protein sits closer to calcium channels at the fast synapses than at the slow ones.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: During short-term strengthening, RIM helps rearrange calcium channels to quickly increase the number of vesicles ready to release.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: The authors note that understanding how RIM works at synapses with different release rates has been hard to figure out before this work.
facts.subject: animals
